title: Any recommendations for applications that allow you to create custom tileset s using elements of existing ones?

posts.author: TheDadGamer
posts.body:
Fast-learning noob here. I'm enjoying piecing together maps in RPG Maker MZ, and have downloaded a small number of great commercial and non-commercial tilesets.
I find myself wishing that I could combine elements of multiple tilesets into a single tileset for use with a specific map. Is there a simple application that can do this?
I'd prefer to not mess around in GIMP if possible, as I'm still in the upwards learning curve for RMMZ. I'm after something quick and convenient, even if I have to pay for it.
Thanks for any advice! This surely has to be one of the last great forums.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
I use this
Characterset Assembler 1.0 by AeroBiba
Rearrange your charactersets easily.
aerobiba.itch.io

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
Aseprite is a powerful yet simple to use graphics tool I use for all my pixelwork. I also have Photoshop, but since Aseprite is specialized on pixel art, it does a much better job for me.
So, if you're willing to spend a few bucks, I can recommend it. Especially, if you invest like 20 minutes in a "tips and tricks for beginnes" type of video.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
You can use Aseprite for free if you compile it yourself. The official website even says you can. There are guides on YouTube and tools to do it.
IF you buy it, you get the pre-compiled exe file and customer support over email but it's not legally required to use it.

posts.author: Norintha
posts.body: I use pixelorama it's free but it's still on a 0. Build.

posts.author: callmedan
posts.body: What about Photopea, it’s a free web-based editor. If you prefer something simpler, Aseprite is a good one

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body: I know you say you don't want to mess with GIMP, but it's my favorite program for making my tilesets. I find most other programs frustrating these days XD The individual layer boundaries make it a breeze to line up pieces in the same place on the grid from tileset to tileset. The tools you use for that particular job are very straightforward--it's almost all copy and paste--it should be pretty quick to learn!
